# Final consolidated MSR retention + semantic-prefetch evidence through attempt 27

## Release question and decision

Provider claim under test: combined MSR retention plus causal semantic prefetch reduces authoritative executed prompt work or attributable GPU model-runner time per completed request versus matched ARC and LRU demand controls, while exact outputs hold and median TTFT regresses no more than 3%. FIFO-prefetch R isolates semantic selection from generic prefetch. Every accepted DRAM arm uses native `store_threshold=2`.

No provider benefit is demonstrated. The three-seed reference supplement repeats a small but exact work regression: M executes 256 more prompt tokens than A/L/R in every 48-request trace (+0.21348%), and uses 0.44660 s more model-runner time than A on average (small-sample normal-approximation 95% interval [0.42528, 0.46792] s) and 0.45799 s more than L ([0.43986, 0.47613] s). The individual seed results and consistent negative direction are primary; n=3 does not support broad population-precision claims. M's semantic nomination is fresh and constrained, but it chooses the no-return source and wastes all 7,340,032 staged bytes in each trace. On the genuinely disjoint trace M chooses a returning source and consumes all staged bytes, but executed work merely ties A/L/R and model-runner time is +4.94% versus A, +5.13% versus L, and +0.31% versus R. Thus useful movement alone still does not produce downstream provider benefit.

GPU-time scope: these are instrumented TP1 current-stream model-runner intervals with one end-event synchronization per step. DMA may overlap and is not added as disjoint work; this is not an uninstrumented production-cost estimate.

This rules out the tested revisions/inputs as release-benefit evidence; it does not rule out MSR provider benefits generally. The repeated interval covers one input cohort under seeds 1103/2207/3301. The disjoint cohort is one additional seed and is reported separately, not pooled into the reference interval.

Total accepted here is 40 valid cells and 1,944/1,944 successful terminal request rows. The v5c source and supplement source are not pooled into an uncertainty interval. The a26 and a27 supplement uses runtime `f3f036805c886c562d1b5397da40a898f163e93a`, analyzer SHA-256 `a64ff49cc8d225b22ef9b0775303456856281f88e1a9f8dc289e93de90886e28`, and frozen bundle SHA-256 `6d3564a211a8aed0bc291890e61d05a84da8deaa6d87c11bcad994c7d0e32cd0`.

The disjoint proof reports empty intersections for all six frozen identity fields: `source_id`, `source_sha256`, `input_sha256`, `context_sha256`, `known_prefix_token_digest`, and `prompt_token_digest`. Its working set is not pooled with reference. All accepted comparisons match request manifest, baseline profile, model/runtime, scheduler, DRAM/GPU budgets, admission, arrival order, and generic machinery within the trace. Exact policy-specific residency is allowed to evolve. Output-token and key-chain sequences are equal across A/L/R/M in every accepted profile/replicate.

## A27 genuinely disjoint input

All four cells are valid/exact, 48/48 complete, drain-clean, and have complete v3 accounting. M has fresh causal two-source constrained selection, stages one 16-block / 7,340,032-byte job, completes and consumes all bytes with zero failure, discard, or uncompleted bytes. R also stages and consumes 7,340,032 bytes. M's combined activation is therefore true, unlike the a26 wrong-target traces.

H2D is equal across arms because useful prefetch replaces demand-load traffic rather than reducing total transferred bytes. There is only one disjoint trace, so its interval/SD is unavailable.

## Earlier v5c profile suite: resource, horizon, and load findings

The 24-cell a18/a20/a21/a22/a23/a24+a25 aggregation remains authoritative for profiles not repeated in a26. All 1,176 requests are exact and successful with complete cell-total GPU work. It is not pooled with a26 because the source revision differs.

- Reference, lower-memory, larger-workset, short-horizon, and long-horizon M all execute +0.186% to +0.214% more work than A/L/R. Burst M ties A, is +1.104% worse than L, and is -0.293% better than R on tokens, but is +8.869%/+7.204%/+5.191% worse on model-runner time versus A/L/R.
- Event-authoritative DRAM occupancy reaches the exact configured ceiling in every profile: 469,762,048 B normally and 234,881,024 B in lower memory. Sparse phase samples that suggested only ~128 blocks are not authoritative. No physical displacement identities were emitted, so a retention/displacement or capacity-frontier claim is still unavailable.
- Fixed 1,000 ms accounting has 324 observations, 320 passes, four burst failures, 300 eligible exact contexts, and zero timely full-prefix contexts. R's partial-prefix consumption does not satisfy the full-prefix useful-yield numerator.
- Short and long horizons each have 52 observations across arms, 52 known-survival outcomes, four survivors, zero timely reuse, and zero censored returns. The controlled target has four completed intervening requests. Actual gaps extend to 3.414 s short and 16.128 s long. R consumes while M wastes its staged bytes in both profiles.
- Burst uses eight releases inside 1.019 ms or less, observed concurrency A/L/R/M 12/14/13/14, and burst TTFT p50/max 923.12/1401.56, 920.53/1399.95, 949.18/1448.17, 951.68/1447.22 ms. Recovery TTFT p50/max is 100.22/385.67, 100.01/378.90, 104.36/410.11, 103.66/410.22 ms. Burst cell-total GPU work is complete; singleton-prefill attribution is partial and remains null.

The full 24-row serving/resource table, exact M-A/L/R changes, byte-time integrals, store bytes, queue/service, and prefetch overhead are preserved in `analysis-owner/all-metrics-through-a25-v1/REPORT.md`.

## Complete measurement-category accounting

| Category | Status and numerator/denominator |
|---|---|
| Authoritative executed work | Complete for 1,944/1,944 accepted requests. A26 M is +256 tokens in 3/3 traces; A27 M ties controls. |
| GPU-only reuse / DRAM restore | Complete per request. A26 M loses 256 GPU-reuse tokens per trace with equal 2,064 DRAM tokens; A27 all arms tie at 4,272 / 8,240. |
| Exact cohorts | First observation, first return, repeated return, and no-return/censored structures retained per request; exact output/key-chain equality gates pass in all 40 accepted cells. |
| TTFT / ITL / E2E | Full TTFT/E2E p50/p95/p99/worst and counts. ITL is 28/28 eligible requests per accepted 48-request cell; single-token requests are inapplicable, not missing. |
| Queue / service / episode | Queue/service distributions, makespan, output/request throughput, release lateness, offered/realized rates retained. All accepted drains complete; failures, timeouts, and preemptions are 0. |
| Causal nomination | M records fresh real-worker/query scores, two distinct exact sources, 254 eligible blocks > budget 16, a constrained choice, and exact selected identities. A26 chooses no-return; A27 chooses return. |
| Coalescing and lifecycle | Hint publication, coalescing, decision, submit, completion, staging, bind/install/fence/usable, consumption/retirement retained. A26 M consumes 0/22,020,096 B across 3 traces and wastes all; a26 R consumes 22,020,096/22,020,096. A27 M and R each consume 7,340,032/7,340,032. |
| Physical jobs/bytes | Exactly one successful speculative job per M/R trace; zero failed/uncompleted jobs. DMA device time remains separate from model-runner time. |
| Policy overhead/stalls | A26 M nomination elapsed 36.633/37.046/37.455 ms over 1,046/1,039/1,043 polls. Request-usable/exposed-stall fields are available only when lifecycle evidence supports them; missing values are null, never zero. |
| Occupancy/byte-time | Event-authoritative DRAM and GPU peaks/integrals retained. A26 DRAM peak 469,762,048 B and GPU peak 302 blocks; a27 DRAM peak 469,762,048 B and GPU peak 272. Shared physical blocks are counted once. |
| Fixed-target useful yield | A26: 156/156 service observations pass, 0/144 eligible full-prefix contexts timely. A27: 48/52 pass, 0/48 eligible full-prefix contexts timely. No capacity frontier follows from zero-yield samples. |
| TTL/intervening traffic | Measured in a23 as above: explicit actual gaps, completed intervening traffic, 8/104 arm-horizon survivors, 0/104 timely, 0 censored. Not a production TTL promise. |
| GPU resources | V3 TP1 current-stream model-runner intervals are complete in all accepted cells, with one end-event synchronization per step; these are instrumented measurements, not an uninstrumented production-cost estimate. Non-burst singleton prefill is complete. Burst prefill-only subtotal is null because prompt attribution is partial. DMA may overlap and transfer overlap is not added as disjoint work. |
| Load/burst/recovery | Offered/realized load, <1.019 ms burst span, concurrency, drain, and four-request recovery measured in exact A25 + L/M/R A24 pairing. |
| Traffic/store | H2D and GPU-to-DRAM store bytes retained as overhead. They are not provider cache-write price. |
| CPU/RSS/index resources | Unavailable: no process CPU, RSS byte-time, or index-memory observations. |
| Displacement | Unavailable: no exact physical displacement identity/consequence events, despite DRAM reaching configured capacity. Observation-tracker eviction counters are not physical-KV eviction counters. |
| Price/cost | Unavailable: no explicit price basis; cost/request and dollar savings remain null. |
| Capacity frontier | Unavailable: only a matched high/low sampled contrast, zero full-prefix yield, and no physical displacement attribution; no multi-point frontier. |
| Uncertainty/disjoint | A26 supplies 3 matched seed-level pairs and normal intervals on one input cohort. A27 proves six-field disjointness but has n=1; it is not pooled. |

## Valid negatives, invalid attempts, and cleanup

Attempts 2-4 are inactive/insufficient activation diagnostics; a5 is a single-source mechanism success; a6+a9 is an exact activated four-arm negative; a8 is an exact but source/profile-incompatible A/L continuation and is excluded; a10 improves useful semantic allocation by 12.5% versus FIFO but not downstream work. Attempts 11-17 preserve successive execution/accounting failures or superseded diagnostics: a11 invalid A/inactive stale scoring, a12 warmup CUDA fault, a13 partial GPU accounting, a14 invalid preservation count/stale timing, a15 callback failure, a16 timing unavailable, a17 binding mismatch cancellation. A19 has no cell due an existing-freeze failure. Attempt 24 A is invalid and is replaced only by exact-source A25. None are pooled with accepted cells. Attempts 1, 7, 12, 15, 17, and 19 produced no valid cell; their logs and archives remain retained.

The execution ledger through a27 records 27 supervisors, 73 result artifacts / 4,172 rows, of which 69 cells / 3,980 rows are valid across the entire historical campaign. Supervisor envelope is 3,329.763 s and the measured child-under-lease lower bound is 3,324.551 s; exact lease duration is unavailable. A26 and a27 each have supervisor/run/stage/manifest/capture/retrieve status 0 and empty `cleanup_live_pids`. The standalone `FINAL-CLEANUP.md` and independent audit record the latest post-a27 check: the RTX 5080 lease was free, utilization was 0%, and no owned compute or supervisor process remained. No GPU action was performed by this analysis.

## Completion gaps and next decision

The requested test implementation, matched A/L/R comparisons, exactness checks, activated semantic lifecycle, resource/horizon/load profiles, three-seed reference uncertainty, and a disjoint input are delivered. The release objective remains incomplete because no repeatable provider benefit exists in the measured traces.

Evidence still unavailable for broader claims: physical displacement attribution, multi-point useful-capacity frontier, process CPU/RSS/index memory, price-based cost, production-scale TTL, and an independent repeated beneficial regime. A27 confirms useful semantic consumption on disjoint inputs but has one trace and no downstream benefit. Further repetitions of the current wrong-target reference are not decision-critical. The next bounded implementation should improve causal discrimination without future labels and/or make useful prefetched blocks request-usable earlier; only after a CPU-frozen change should the smallest exact A/L/R/M reference be rerun, then independently confirmed if it shows a real benefit.
